description: Shared parity vectors for the report's display rule (DEL-08-01 Design report-package-current-results.md section 2.3 item 6 and its display resolution; exact-route-report-sections.md section 3.3): the desktop's displayQuantity (apps/desktop/src/features/report/reportQuantityDisplay.ts, vitest reportQuantityDisplay.parity.test.ts) and the report package's quantity_display::display_quantity (core/reporting/report_package/src/quantity_display.rs, test tests/quantity_display_parity.rs) must both turn value and unit into display. The rule starts from the value's ECMAScript Number-to-String text; a value stored in Pa is shifted six decimal places as text and labelled MPa; the decimal significand is rounded to six significant digits, half away from zero, on its digits; the result is printed in the ECMAScript Number-to-String layout; 0 and -0 print 0. No floating-point arithmetic. Each vector states its reason. Values are binary64 numbers both readers parse alike (no integer above 2^53 - 1 that is not a float literal, which Rust would keep exactly and JavaScript would round). Hand-written; invented values only, except the witness headlines, which are the committed witnesses' stored values.

vectors.reason: Witness headline (pressure-2 straight): Pa shown in MPa, rounded to six significant digits; the seventh digit 0 rounds down.
Witness headline (pressure-2 load/reference states): Pa shown in MPa; seventh digit 2 rounds down.
Witness headline (pressure-source-1 load/reference): a value of a few Pa stays plain decimal in MPa (decimal point position -4); seventh digit 9 rounds up.
A stored MPa element stress (pressure-free route) is not scaled; rounded to six significant digits.
Fewer than six significant digits: unchanged.
Zero in Pa prints 0, labelled MPa.
Negative zero prints 0 (as ECMAScript Number-to-String).
Negative zero in an unscaled unit prints 0.
1 Pa is 0.000001 MPa: the last plain-decimal position (decimal point position -5).
Below 1 Pa the shifted value falls under 1e-6 MPa and switches to the exponent form.
Rounding carry across the small exponent switch: 9.999995e-7 MPa rounds up to 1e-6 MPa, which is plain decimal again.
The same carry unscaled: 9.999995e-7 rounds to 0.000001.
Unscaled value below 1e-6 keeps the ECMAScript exponent form.
Unscaled 1e-6 is plain decimal (ECMAScript).
A value below 1 Pa: shifted six places as text.
Negative Pa value: sign kept, shifted.
Rounding carry in Pa: 0.9999995 MPa rounds half away from zero to 1 MPa.
Just below the carry: the seventh digit 4 rounds down.
Negative rounding carry: half away from zero on the magnitude.
Rounding carry in a unit that is not Pa: 999999.5 rounds to 1000000.
Half-way tie (seventh digit 5, nothing after): rounds away from zero.
Negative tie rounds away from zero.
Tie on an even sixth digit: half away from zero gives 12.3457 (half-to-even would give 12.3456).
Tie on an odd sixth digit rounds up.
Below the tie: rounds down, trailing zeros dropped.
Tie with the decimal point before the first digit.
Binary-to-decimal noise is rounded away; the stored value is unchanged.
The same value in Pa shifts below 1e-6 MPa: exponent form.
Largest safe integer: rounded to six significant digits, zeros fill the integer part.
Largest safe integer in Pa: shifted and rounded.
Negative value with nine integer digits rounds to six significant digits.
Smallest subnormal: exponent form unchanged.
Smallest subnormal in Pa: the shift is exact on the text, beyond binary64's range.
At 1e21 ECMAScript switches to the exponent form with an explicit sign.
Rounding carry across the large exponent switch: 9.999999999999999e20 rounds to 1e21, exponent form.
Just below the large switch: plain decimal with 21 digits.
1e21 Pa is 1e15 MPa, plain decimal after the shift.
1e26 Pa is 1e20 MPa: plain decimal, 21 digits.
1e27 Pa is 1e21 MPa: the exponent form after the shift.
Rounding carry across the large switch after the shift: 9.999995e20 MPa rounds to 1e21 MPa.
Largest binary64: rounded in exponent form.
Largest binary64 in Pa: shifted in the exponent.
Six significant digits: unchanged.
Seven integer digits: rounded, a zero fills the integer part.
A dimensionless count keeps its unit text.
A non-ASCII unit is kept verbatim; plain decimal.
